newsitem.title: CANADA: Talisman to extend Wascana offer.
newsitem.headline: Talisman to extend Wascana offer.

text.p: Talisman Energy Inc, currently the low bidder in a takeover battle for Wascana Energy Inc, planned to extend the expiry date of its offer, a Talisman spokesman said on Monday.
Talisman's hostile C$1.7 billion cash and stock bid for Regina, Saskatchewan-based Wascana was to have expired today.

Talisman's Dave Mann said in a phone interview that he could not confirm the new expiry date. But it was likely it would be about the same date as the expiry of a C$2 billion offer from white knight Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd, he said.
CanOxy's C$20.50 a share cash offer expires 21 days after the mailing of the offering circular, which was also expected today.
Mann said Talisman continued to request access to Wascana's confidential financial and operating data in the wake of CanOxy's bid, but to no avail.
A sticking point was the Wascana board's assertion that Talisman must up its offer before getting through the data room door.
Talisman Chief Executive Jim Buckee has said several times that his firm might be prepared to pay more if it could be sure Wascana's oil and gas assets had more value than was previously thought.
Talisman opened the bidding in February by offering C$18.50 cash or 0.41 of a Talisman share for each Wascana share. Wascana's board rejected the advance and struck a deal last week with CanOxy.
One analyst said he believed it was unlikely Talisman would be the victor in the race to absorb Wascana, a former government-owned oil company known mostly for its vast heavy oil reserves.
"I think there's a fair amount of stock in arb hands, and these guys want cash, they don't want stock," Bob Hinckley, an analyst with Merrill Lynch in New York, said on Monday.
"So, Talisman's going to have to come up with an all-cash offer, I think, to carry the day and I just don't see how they can do it with the balance sheet they've got."
However, Hinckley said Wascana's share price, which was C$0.10 above CanOxy's offer on Monday, suggested there was still market speculation about a higher bid.

Chances still existed for a third bidder to enter the fray, possibly for the United States, because of Wascana's potential for sharply higher low-risk oil and gas production and its location in the growing Saskatchewan energy sector, he said. "I wouldn't be surprised if somebody came along with a competing bid but I don't think it's going to be Talisman."
Wascana shares on Monday were up 0.05 to 20.60 on volume of 518,155 shares. Talisman climbed 0.40 to 43.40, while CanOxy extended its post-bid rise by 0.30 to trade at 27.10.
